title: Improvements for dividend loading functionality
body:
The Issue tracker is **ONLY** used for reporting bugs. New features should be discussed in our [Slack](https://join.slack.com/t/ghostfolio/shared_invite/zt-vsaan64h-F_I0fEo5M0P88lP9ibCxFg) community or in [Discussions](https://github.com/ghostfolio/ghostfolio/discussions).

**Bug Description**

The dividend loading functionality looks great. But there are a few Issues with dividend loading functionality:

1. The activity date appears to be the ex-dividend date rather than the payment date. I think the payment date should be used as that will be useful for tax purposes, I am not sure if the ex-date is of much value afterwards?
2. Dividends are added without the correct account mapping IF there are multiple transactions across different accounts. The dividends across accounts for the same date are combined and added as a single entry without an account, which is incorrect. I will describe how to reproduce this below. 

**To Reproduce**

<!-- Steps to reproduce the behavior -->

I have attached a zip file with 2 buy transaction JSON files to help reproduce this issue. Please edit the files to add a different account ID to each file first.
[activities.zip](https://github.com/ghostfolio/ghostfolio/files/11971901/activities.zip)

1. Import file act1.json  to import the first transaction
2. Without fully importing, just load dividends for BERI.L - the preview shows the correct account mapping (screenshot 1). Cancel the prompt, don't load the dividend activity.
3. Now import file act2.json to import the second transaction against a different account ID
4. Now go back to Import Dividends and load dividends - the account column is blank (screenshot 2).
5. Also, instead of showing 8 activities, it only shows 4 as it has combined the dividends for the same date together.
6. Complete the import, accounts are blank in the activity list  (screenshot 3).


**Expected behavior**

1. Activity date should be the payment date rather than ex-dividend date
2. Accounts should be correctly mapped in case of the same holding being present across multiple accounts.
3. Dividend amounts shouldn't be combined if they are paid into different accounts - assume this will work correctly if above is fixed.
